Configuration objects should be registered as singletons.

What The Standard says

“Configuration Models” — The Standard places application configuration in the composition boundary rather than business services. Registering a completed configuration object there gives consumers one stable instance. read it here.
“fully encapsulated” — The library-composition example encapsulates dependency injection and registers its configuration as a singleton. The analyser makes that demonstrated lifetime the default for configuration objects. read it here.

Why it matters

Configuration represents one application-wide interpretation of startup input. Registering it as a singleton ensures every service observes the same immutable setup and avoids repeatedly rebuilding or inconsistently binding configuration throughout the dependency graph.

Bad code example

// Violates STXAPP003: Configuration objects should be registered as singletons.
services.AddScoped<SchoolConfiguration>();

Good code example

// Follows STXAPP003
services.AddSingleton<SchoolConfiguration>();
